=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:244-294, 308-314 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The extractor accepts the first complete chain even when a newer V2 write is incomplete or malformed, so an older failed state can be returned as current.
  WHY: A torn newer write can cause the judge to record a close verdict and apply ai:unblock-closed, allowing the poller to abandon an active project.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:94-106 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_trusted_project_status()` calls the extractor without `--require-latest`, allowing it to accept an older complete state after a newer V2 write is incomplete.
  WHY: Even if the extractor supported `--require-latest`, this call site would not use it, leaving the stale-state failure possible.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:182-188 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The terminal recheck combines fetch failure, untrusted state extraction failure, and project state change into one `reason=project_state_changed_before_terminal_label` log entry.
  WHY: Operators and log analysis tooling cannot distinguish a transient API error, a trust-boundary violation, and a genuine project-state change.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:182-192 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `ensure_label_exists` runs after the terminal recheck, leaving a window before the label POST in which a project can resume without being rechecked.
  WHY: A project that resumes during the label-catalog API call can still have ai:unblock-closed applied, letting the poller abandon an active project.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  confidence=[5]

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:244-294, 308-314 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The extractor has no --require-latest mechanism. It walks comments newest-first, accepts the first complete chain regardless of whether a newer V2 write is incomplete or malformed, and returns it. A newer partial chunk (e.g. 2-part write with only part 1 posted) is silently skipped when an older complete failed state exists below it.
  WHY: An unlabeled project whose state-posting was torn can have its older complete failed state returned by the extractor, the judge records a close verdict and applies ai:unblock-closed, and the poller abandons the active project. The docstring at lines 23-26 still carries the legacy description without the --require-latest documentation that the PR DIFF claims to add. The grep for require-latest across scripts/*.py returns zero matches.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:94-106 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The extractor call at lines 102-103 passes only --comments-json without --require-latest. The function comment at lines 94-95 states "No V1 or untrusted-comment fallback is safe for this decision" but the implementation uses the legacy fallback path that silently accepts an older complete state when a newer V2 write is incomplete.
  WHY: Even if the extractor supported --require-latest, this call site would not use it. The legacy extractor behavior accepts the first complete chain found, which can be an older failed state after a newer write was torn. The grep for require-latest across scripts/unblock_judge.sh returns zero matches.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:182-188 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The terminal recheck uses a combined || chain that conflates three distinct failure modes (fetch failure, untrusted state extraction failure, project state changed) into one reason=project_state_changed_before_terminal_label log entry. The last_run_diff claims to split these into three distinct reason strings (project_state_terminal_recheck_unavailable, project_state_terminal_unverified, project_state_changed_before_terminal_label) but the on-disk code does not.
  WHY: Operators and log analysis tooling cannot distinguish between a transient API error, a trust-boundary violation, and a genuine project-state change from the terminal-recheck log line. All three collapse to the same label.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:182-192 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: ensure_label_exists (lines 190-192) runs AFTER the terminal recheck (lines 182-188). A project that resumes during ensure_label_exists is not rechecked before the label POST at line 193. The last_run_diff claims to move the recheck after label-catalog preparation, but the on-disk file has the old ordering.
  WHY: The race window between the terminal recheck and the label POST includes the entire ensure_label_exists API call. A project that resumes during that window will still have ai:unblock-closed applied, letting the poller abandon an active project.
- Requirement: "Verify the latest trusted project state is still failed before deciding and again before applying a terminal label; skip stale dispatches or unverifiable state." (issue #6277)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py cmd_extract (the --require-latest flag and latest_chain_key enforcement) and scripts/unblock_judge.sh unblock_trusted_project_status (the --require-latest call argument)
  Evidence of absence: The on-disk extractor at cmd_extract lines 244-294 has no latest_chain_key variable, no args.require_latest check, and no chain_key filtering by latest-chain identity. The main() at lines 308-314 adds no --require-latest argument. The caller at unblock_judge.sh lines 102-103 passes only --comments-json. Grep for require-latest across both scripts returns zero matches. The extractor docstring at orchestrate_state_v2.py lines 23-26 still describes only the legacy fallback behavior.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "The judge's --require-latest read rejects an incomplete or malformed newer write instead of falling back to an older failed state." (agents.md documentation line in the PR DIFF)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py cmd_extract lines 244-294
  Evidence of absence: The on-disk cmd_extract walks comments newest-first at line 244, parses each chunk at line 248, and returns the first complete chain that passes hash verification at lines 282-288. There is no check that rejects a newer incomplete chain in favor of only fresher chains. The unchained fallback the documentation describes as hardened is the runtime behavior of the on-disk code.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "Refuses to treat an older complete failed snapshot as current when a newer V2 state write is incomplete or malformed." (changelog.d fragment)
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py cmd_extract and scripts/unblock_judge.sh unblock_trusted_project_status
  Evidence of absence: Neither file on disk contains the --require-latest mechanism. The extractor at cmd_extract lines 244-294 accepts the first complete chain regardless of whether a newer incomplete write exists above it in comment order. The caller at lines 102-103 uses the legacy fallback path. This is the unguarded legacy behavior the changelog and agents.md claim was hardened; the hardening code does not exist on disk.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: Tests for torn-write resilience, multichunk acceptance, terminal-recheck refusal of older state, label-prep resume, and late resume during judgment
  Expected change site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py new test functions
  Evidence of absence: Grep for test_latest_project_state, test_unlabeled_project_resumes_during_label, test_unlabeled_project_terminal_recheck_refuses, and test_unlabeled_project_recheck_refuses_older returns zero matches. test_unlabeled_project_requires_trusted_v2_state at line 892 has 3 cases instead of 4 (missing the torn-write case). test_unlabeled_project_does_not_label_after_late_resume at line 933 has 2 parametrize parameters instead of 3 (missing reason). The FAKE_GH_ITEM_COMMENTS_AFTER_LABEL_CREATE handler is absent (grep returns zero matches).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
